newsitem.title: INDIA: Southern India petrol stations close for a day.
newsitem.headline: Southern India petrol stations close for a day.

text.p: A day-long strike on Monday kept petrol and diesel retail outlets run by private operators in southern India closed, a spokesman of the striking union said.
The All India Petroleum Traders Federation (AIPTF) had called the strike to press for an increase in sales commissions to five percent from one percent.

AIPTF also wants the exclusion of petroleum products from the Essential Commodities Act, which allows government control on supply of key consumer goods, and compensation for product losses arising from temperature variations.
"Our demand for more commission has been hanging fire for more than a year. None of the oil corporations have responded. It is time the government acted," said T. Harinarayana, AIPTF secretary.
The strike was the third called recently by private petroleum dealers in India. The first was in the western state of Maharashtra on July 3 and the second in northern India on August 4.
Nirmal Kumar, vice-president of AIPTF, said if the government did not take action on its demands, the federation would meet in Delhi on August 30 to decide on further measures.
Devi Dayal, a senior official in the Petroleum Ministry said the dealers' strike was unjustified.
"The strike is against the interest of the consumers," Dayal told Reuters.
He said a panel of directors of state-run oil companies had finalised a report on dealers' commissions. "The government will take a decision once the report is submitted."
